subject: Allow parentheses in executable paths (External Tools, custom PuTTY path)
body:
Allow parentheses in executable paths (External Tools, custom PuTTY path)

PathValidator.IsValidExecutablePath rejected any path containing '('
or ')' as a "dangerous shell metacharacter", citing command-injection
risk. But every path validated here (External Tools FileName,
IntegratedProgram's executable, PuttyBase.PuttyPath) is launched with
UseShellExecute=false, going straight to CreateProcess with no shell
parsing - parentheses in a file path are inert there.

This made the External Tools feature (and a custom PuTTY path) unusable
for anything installed under the standard "C:\Program Files (x86)\..."
location - e.g. WinSCP. Adding a WinSCP external tool failed with
"Invalid executable path: path contains potentially dangerous
characters" and silently logged the error.

Removed '(' and ')' from the dangerous-character set; kept the actual
shell control/redirection characters (&|;<>^ and CR/LF), which have no
legitimate place in a file path regardless of how it's launched.

security_flags.reason: added code spawns a process or evaluates a string as code

triage.rationale: Our PathValidator.cs:65 already excludes parentheses with identical char set and same Program Files (x86) rationale. Fully covered.
